notes.meaning: Solomon begins a new collection of short proverbs that contrast wisdom with folly. A child who learns wisdom and walks with God brings deep gladness to both parents. A child who rejects guidance brings heavy grief, especially to the mother who cared for him.

Possessions gained by cheating, stealing, or violence provide no lasting benefit in the day of trouble. Money cannot buy peace with God or stop physical death. Doing what is right before the Lord delivers a person from spiritual ruin and the sting of death.

The Lord watches over those who love Him and promises to supply what their lives truly need. Even in times of hardship, He sustains their souls. At the same time, He frustrates the greedy appetites of wicked people who push Him away.

Laziness and half-hearted effort naturally lead toward poverty and hardship. In contrast, steady and focused work brings stability and provision. God usually chooses to bless honest, energetic labor rather than neglect.

A wise child understands when important work must be done and gathers the crops while the weather is good. Someone who sleeps through the harvest wastes a golden opportunity that will not return. Such laziness brings poverty and public shame on the entire household.

God and community members shower favors and good words upon people who live upright lives. These blessings rest on the godly like an honorable crown. Evil people, however, hide cruel and violent schemes behind their smooth speech.

Good people leave behind a legacy that continues to encourage and inspire others long after they pass away. People speak of them with warmth and gratitude. The reputation of an evil person rots away like garbage and is remembered only with disgust.

A person with a truly wise heart gladly listens to God's commands and welcomes godly correction. People who only babble and boast think they already know everything. Their careless, argumentative talk will soon bring them crashing down.

Living with honesty and pure motives gives a person deep security. Because such a person has nothing hidden, they walk through life without fear of exposure. Anyone who chooses dishonest shortcuts will eventually be discovered and brought to justice.

A person who winks slyly behind someone's back is usually plotting trouble in secret. That sneaky cruelty causes genuine pain to others. At the same time, a foolish person who talks recklessly also brings ruin upon themselves.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that ancient translations like the Septuagint read the second line as 'he who rebukes boldly makes peace,' contrasting hidden malice with honest, open correction.

notes.meaning: The words of a godly person refresh and encourage others like a spring of clean, cool water. They bring comfort to the hurting and direction to the confused. The wicked may speak polite words, but underneath they hide hurtful, violent intentions.

Bitterness and hatred look for excuses to start arguments and stir up old quarrels. Love chooses a completely different path by forgiving wrongs and refusing to gossip about another person's failures. Forgiving love quietly protects peace in the community.

People with good understanding speak with discernment and offer helpful advice. Those who reject wisdom refuse to learn through words. Because they will not listen, painful physical discipline and hard consequences become their only teacher.

Sensible people quietly store up true knowledge like treasure in a storeroom, waiting for the right moment to share it. Fools simply blurt out whatever thought pops into their minds. Their loose talk constantly invites conflict and destruction.

In practical life, money can shield a wealthy person from many sudden dangers and disasters. In contrast, extreme poverty leaves people helpless, friendless, and open to mistreatment. This observation highlights the real hardships that poor people face every day.

The honest work of a good person aims at providing for life and blessing others, which leads to genuine peace. The income of an evil person is used to feed selfish pleasures and sinful habits. That kind of gain only produces guilt and judgment.

Anyone who welcomes instruction and obeys good advice stays on the road that leads to true life. A person who bristles at correction and ignores warnings wanders off that path. By doing so, they also lead others into trouble.

A person who hides hatred behind sweet words and false smiles is acting like a liar. Someone who openly runs around telling slanderous stories is acting like a fool. Both kinds of talk show an unhealthy, deceitful heart.

When people talk endlessly, they almost always end up saying things that are hurtful, boastful, or untrue. A truly wise person learns to rein in their tongue. Holding back words prevents countless misunderstandings and sins.

The speech of a righteous person is precious and refined like pure silver, giving great value to those who listen. The inner thoughts and character of a wicked person are worthless dross. What comes out of a person shows what is inside.

The wise words of a godly person feed and strengthen the souls of many people, just as a shepherd feeds his flock. Fools lack even the basic judgment needed to protect themselves. Because they reject wisdom, they bring about their own destruction.

Real, lasting wealth comes when the Lord gives His blessing, not from human anxiety and scheming alone. When God gives good things, He does not add the misery, guilt, and fear that come with ill-gotten gain. His gifts bring true peace of mind.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern prosperity teachers use this proverb to promise that every faithful believer is entitled to financial wealth without hardship.

notes.meaning: A foolish person treats wrongdoing and harmful pranks like an amusing game. They laugh at sin instead of feeling shame for it. A person with true understanding finds their real delight in acting with wisdom and doing what is right.

Wicked people often live with hidden fears of disaster and judgment, and those very terrors will one day overtake them. The righteous desire goodness, peace, and closeness with God. The Lord will answer those good desires and satisfy their hearts.

When fierce storms of trouble or divine judgment blow through, the wicked are swept completely away like dust. They have nothing stable to hold onto. Those who trust the Lord are built on a solid rock that will never be destroyed.

Drinking sour vinegar sets teeth on edge, and thick smoke stings the eyes and makes them water. A lazy worker sent on an errand causes that exact kind of pain and annoyance to the person who sent him. Reliable help is essential for any task.

Deep reverence and love for God encourage a healthy, peaceful way of living that often leads to a long life. Turning toward God keeps a person away from dangerous, destructive habits. Wicked living often cuts life short through violence and excess.

The patient hope of the righteous leads to lasting joy because God will faithfully fulfill His promises to them. In contrast, the greedy hopes and proud plans of the wicked will crumble to dust. What evil people count on will leave them empty.

The path of God's commands acts like a strong fortress for anyone who walks with integrity. Obeying the Lord keeps them safe under His care. But that very same holy standard brings ruin to those who stubbornly practice evil.

Those who walk faithfully with God will never be shaken from His love or His eternal home. They enjoy a secure place in His kingdom. The wicked may seem powerful for a moment, but they will be uprooted and lose all claim to the land.

The words of a righteous person produce healthy, life-giving wisdom, much like a good tree bearing sweet fruit. A perverse tongue that constantly twists the truth brings poison instead of nourishment. That kind of speech will eventually be cut down and silenced.

A godly person understands what is fitting, helpful, and pleasing to both God and neighbors before speaking. Their words bring grace to the room. The mouth of the wicked, however, pours out only twisted and rude talk that causes strife.
